blocks.text: The census begins at Sinai, the starting point of the book’s movement. Numbers will proceed through Kadesh and the Transjordan toward the plains of Moab; Egypt remains the land Israel has left rather than the principal setting of the narrative.

This opening census is part of the book’s larger structure. Numbers 1 counts the generation at Sinai, while a later census in Numbers 26 counts the generation prepared for inheritance near Moab. The two censuses therefore frame the transition between these generations as the narrative moves from preparation at Sinai toward preparation on the plains of Moab.

sections.title: The Census and the Book’s Shape

blocks.text: The size of the census total, and its implications for Israel’s wilderness population, has received substantially different literary and historical interpretations. The chapter clearly presents its total, but deciding how that figure should be reconstructed historically remains disputed; the text should not be made to settle that question without acknowledging the uncertainty.
